Title: Confirm three-member access and standalone workflow
User story: As a teammate, I want my own account and a reproducible local setup so I can choose a task, contribute a reviewed change and verify its deployment.
Acceptance criteria:
Each member confirms access to toecm/factoryrelay through their own GitHub account and records a successful clone/install/test/build on their computer.
Use FactoryRelay as the project root. Confirm the research folder is local-only and agree an approved sharing location for course documents without participant data or credentials.
Agree branch and pull-request review conventions; record one reviewed change and check its GitHub CI and Vercel deployment result. Do not assume a GitHub invitation grants Vercel or private Space access.
Record who publishes the private personal-account Space and public fictional dataset. Keep present visibility and owner-managed publication; no new account-sharing or automatic data upload.
Deliverable: Three-member access/setup checklist; reviewed contribution evidence; project-path and publishing responsibilities note.

Title: Build a traceable literature matrix
User story: As a student researcher, I want a reproducible search and critical evidence matrix so our design choices can be checked against previous work.
Acceptance criteria:
Search log records search date, databases/sites, exact queries, filters and inclusion/exclusion rules; screen peer-reviewed/primary technical work, including local translation/adaptation, retrieval/personalization, human clarification and industrial communication simulation.
Start from proposal citations but verify bibliographic fields and actual claimed findings against the original sources. Unverifiable citations stay flagged and are excluded from evidence claims.
By the end of Sprint 1, include at least eight directly relevant primary papers/systems with source, task/languages, data/split, baseline, method, metrics, limitations and availability/license. Continue refinement in R02 toward 12 screened items; if fewer qualify, document the search rather than add weak matches.
Second team member checks at least 4 included studies and every study used to justify the closest-work or novelty comparison.
Deliverable:
Literature matrix CSV/XLSX
Search log and screening counts
Verified bibliography

Title: Choose one reviewed language scope and prove the local runtime path
User story: As a pilot participant, I want a declared source-to-target language or variety pair and a tested device profile so that supported translation is based on evidence rather than an unrestricted language selector.
Acceptance criteria:
Record the first translation direction, task vocabulary, named reviewer role/availability and intended language-variety coverage. Distinguish speaker-reviewed regional usage from company jargon and code-switching.
Benchmark a small, predeclared development set on the actual initial devices; record checkpoint/runtime/license, peak memory, latency, loading time and example operational-field errors. Agree numerical latency/memory targets before the final acceptance run; do not invent a passed quality threshold.
Demonstrate one offline inference request through the proposed device-local companion connection, including the browser/HTTPS/CSP boundary, with outside-network requests blocked. Record one feasible local integration route or a clear failed feasibility gate.
Name at least one laptop eligible for a training experiment and the second device's supported inference mode. Record minimum reviewed-data requirements and resource checks for training; an unsupported phone has an explicit original-text/clarification path. Timebox the spike to eight team hours; attempt one tiny adapter update on synthetic data where compatible. Record actual changed-weight evidence or a failed gate, not a promised future capability.
Deliverable: Capability matrix, model/license record, benchmark CSV and one local-only request trace.

Title: Validate the existing LAN game on two physical devices
User story: As a classroom pair, I want the current room to work on our actual devices without internet so that the known browser prototype is ready to receive translation features.
Acceptance criteria:
From the standalone FactoryRelay root, use the existing launcher on two physical devices to verify the host's local certificate, create/join a room, complete a round and export with the router WAN link disconnected; save device/browser/network details. The previous browser-context checks do not satisfy this acceptance condition.
Repeat the basic round on the intended hotspot with internet access disabled while local peer communication remains available. Record a hotspot's isolation restriction as a failed configuration, not as a passed offline test.
Interrupt one device, reconnect in its original tab and retry an uncertain action; verify no duplicate decision/message, no role takeover and correct held-versus-executed reporting.
Record host-stop and restart behavior accurately: shared actions pause, RAM rooms are lost on restart, and a separate loaded pass-and-play session does not restore the LAN room.
Deliverable: Signed physical-device checklist, configuration matrix, export files and defect/retest record.

Title: Test the contribution against the closest work
User story: As the team, we want to identify the closest existing systems so our originality claim is specific, testable and appropriately limited.
Acceptance criteria:
Choose 3-5 closest prior systems using explicit criteria: task, human-review loop, adaptation mechanism, on-device execution and evaluation setting.
Feature/evidence table distinguishes already-known components from the proposed combination and any untested mechanism; absence of a feature in a paper is labeled 'not reported' unless verified.
Write one primary novelty hypothesis and one fallback contribution (e.g. a reproducible operational-semantics benchmark or local adaptation evaluation). Specify what experiment could refute each.
Log a bounded prior-art search over relevant patent databases using keywords and classifications; record dates, queries, identifiers/families, potentially overlapping technical features and search limitations.
Prepare a questions-and-evidence brief for supervisor/technology-transfer review. Do not label the idea patentable or claim exhaustive clearance. Include an inventory and dates of the already public game and fictional dataset so institutional reviewers can assess actual disclosure history; do not state that all material is still private.
Update the verified literature matrix toward 12 relevant items while checking all closest-work claims. Record database/search date and boundaries; this is not an exhaustive patent search.
Deliverable:
Closest-work comparison table
One-page contribution hypothesis
Prior-art search log and institutional-review questions

Title: Freeze a text-first evaluation and data protocol
User story: As an evaluator, I want agreed conditions, labels and data boundaries before collecting results so the comparison is fair and repeatable.
Acceptance criteria:
Protocol fixes one source/target variety pair, translation direction(s), primary operational task, model-selection criteria, intended devices and what counts as a critical error.
Predefine B0/B1/B2 and optional B3, the fixed guided/original-message UI condition, held-out split rules, adaptation timing, primary/secondary metrics and analysis unit.
Rubric covers equipment, action, negation, quantity/unit, condition and timing, plus unsupported additions. Include at least 12 labeled examples and source-uncertainty cases. Use development examples for rubric practice. Declare message-level any-critical-error rate primary and per-field errors diagnostic; keep the final test out of rubric tuning.
Document participant information/consent, recording choices, withdrawal/retention/deletion and host visibility; confirm whether the institution requires review before recruitment or research-data collection.
Both a workflow reviewer and a competent bilingual/target-variety reviewer approve the relevant parts; no unqualified reviewer is treated as language ground truth.
Deliverable:
Versioned evaluation protocol
Annotation rubric
Consent and data-handling materials
Scope/readiness decision

Title: Install and verify an offline text model pack
User story: As a supported-device user, I want a verified local model pack and readiness status so that translation does not unexpectedly depend on internet access.
Acceptance criteria:
A versioned manifest identifies the checkpoint, tokenizer, runtime, license, hashes, sizes and supported profile. The app distinguishes the quantized inference artifact from any later training checkpoint.
After one explicit provisioning step, verify/reuse local artifacts and run a fixed test translation with internet blocked. Readiness reports missing, corrupt or incompatible resources and offers setup guidance; it never silently calls a cloud model.
The device-local companion is reachable only through the approved local connection with scoped authorization/origin checks; the isolated LAN shell does not gain unrestricted external access.
Interruption or a bad checksum leaves the last usable pack intact, and the user can select or remove a pack without corrupting saved game records.
Deliverable: Pack manifest, reproducible provision/start commands, request trace and measured resource log.

Title: Offer per-device consent and a local text-capture vault
User story: As a player, I want to choose whether my own device retains examples for review or training so that playing the game does not automatically create a personal training corpus.
Acceptance criteria:
Before optional persistent capture, show separate choices for gameplay sharing, local example retention and later training. Refusal still permits ordinary play. Explain that the host and recipient already receive shared chat; local deletion cannot revoke their copies or exports.
On each supported device, store only explicitly retained text records in its local vault with source wording, consent/provenance and review status. Capture defaults off; user-private examples are excluded from room messages and shared exports.
Provide inspect, keep/delete and bulk-delete controls. For the supported laptop vault, use the chosen OS-backed key storage/encryption path and verify locked/unavailable-key behavior without exposing plaintext in logs.
Test that restarting the room host neither uploads nor merges the players' private corpora and that unretained examples are not added to the training queue.
Deliverable: Consent screenshots, storage/data-flow checklist and deletion/refusal regression results.

Title: Create a bounded reviewed corpus with protected splits
User story: As an evaluator, I want reviewed operational messages and matched unseen variants so adaptation is measured on new material rather than memorized answers.
Acceptance criteria:
Planning target is 120 short operational utterances across three selected risks: negation, quantity/unit and conditional sequence. Use independent base-case families with reviewed variants; retain all six game scenarios but restrict new linguistic annotation to these three risks. Team confirms workload in Sprint 1 and documents any reduction before testing.
Target split is 60 adaptation/training, 20 development and 40 final-test records. Assign whole base-case families, paraphrase/translation clusters and author/session groups before adaptation; do not split a base case between training and test. Exact counts may be adjusted to preserve groups, with the manifest explaining the change.
Every record has provenance, consent/license status, source/target variety, scenario-family/session ID, original text, speaker-confirmed intended meaning, reviewed target rendering and applicable slot labels.
At least all final-test records receive independent second review followed by adjudication; record agreement and disagreements instead of silently replacing labels.
Keep the final test hidden from model developers until the protocol/harness is frozen. Future game-session corrections are not ingested before their held-out evaluation.
Deliverable:
Locally stored reviewed corpus
Split/provenance manifest
Annotation agreement and adjudication record

Title: Display original and locally translated text during one game round
User story: As a player receiving an unfamiliar message, I want the original and a clearly labelled local translation together so that I can verify details and ask for clarification before deciding.
Acceptance criteria:
In one complete existing scenario, the receiving device translates a sent message for the selected, tested source-to-target pair and displays unchanged original text, generated rendering and its status/model identity.
The translation uses only the message and context visible to that participant; scenario answer IDs, hidden partner facts and scoring explanations are excluded from its request. Test this boundary directly.
Cancel, timeout, missing-pack and unsupported-profile cases keep the original available with clarification controls. Low certainty is presented as an explicit limitation or clarification prompt, not an uncalibrated accuracy percentage.
The scene, shared message ordering and deterministic decision scoring remain intact on both devices; measure the agreed latency/resource targets on the supported profile and retain failures in the report.
Deliverable: Two-device round recording, bilingual example review, prompt-boundary test and latency/resource measurements.

Title: Create analysis-ready exports and matched evaluation fixtures
User story: As a researcher, I want exports to identify the condition, transport and artifact versions so the frozen, glossary, memory and eligible adapter conditions can be compared reproducibly.
Acceptance criteria:
Version the export schema and explicitly record transport kind, build/scenario version, pseudonymous session/device profile, selected language direction, model/runtime/pack version, memory/adapter version, inference location and test condition. Exclude bearer tokens and private training corpora by default.
Implement scenario-variant IDs and the split manifest specified by R03/R04. Validate that near-duplicates and answer keys cannot enter evaluation prompts. Retain the existing six teaching rounds as regression fixtures; R04 owns corpus annotation.
Record original output and reviewer-coded critical-field errors, unsupported additions, decision outcomes, clarification/resolution timing, inference latency and resource measures with definitions. Keep attempted wrong actions distinct from simulator blocks; describe elapsed-time interruption handling.
Implement and validate logging for B0 frozen, B1 fixed approved glossary, B2 retrieved reviewed memory and optional B3 memory plus adapter. A repeatable script validates the exports; R03 owns the protocol and R06 owns final comparison.
Deliverable: Schema contract, split manifest, approved variants, frozen protocol and reproducible summary output.

Title: Review corrections and retrieve approved local examples
User story: As a speaker, I want to review wording and add approved examples to my own local memory so that later translations can use verified terminology without claiming that the model was retrained.
Acceptance criteria:
After a session, selected retained examples can be kept, corrected, approved or deleted. The record separates original text, intended operational meaning and target rendering, with reviewer/provenance and selected language profile.
Only approved, consented examples enter the local retrieval index. Duplicate, withdrawn and unreviewed records are excluded; removing an example removes its retrieval availability.
A later translation can show the retrieved terminology/example provenance. The same frozen model can run with memory disabled or enabled for comparison; base/adapter weight hashes remain unchanged after memory-only updates.
Evaluation holdouts and simulator answer keys cannot enter the approved-memory source. Profiles reflect user selection and speaker review, not inferred demographic stereotypes.
Deliverable: Reviewed example cards, memory-on/off prompt traces, index deletion tests and unchanged model-weight hashes.

Title: Run opt-in post-session LoRA training on one eligible laptop
User story: As an eligible-laptop user, I want a genuine optional adapter-training job after review so that I can experiment with personal adaptation while ordinary play remains available without training.
Acceptance criteria:
After each session, offer keep/delete, memory-only update, queue for later, or train only when the documented local capability/data gate passes. Training is opt-in, uses reviewed selected records and does not run during a live game.
On the one named eligible laptop, complete a local LoRA/PEFT job using the verified training checkpoint. Save configuration, dataset manifest, loss/run log and an adapter artifact; verify adapter weights actually changed while the frozen base remains unchanged.
Ineligible hardware, insufficient reviewed examples, power/storage limits or missing training files leave data queued with a clear reason. No phone-training claim is made without its own successful validation.
Cancellation, resource failure or host/network loss does not replace the active adapter or destroy the last validated model. The training job makes no outside-network request after provisioning.
Deliverable: Eligibility report, approved-data manifest, changed-adapter/unchanged-base hashes, completed run log and failure-recovery checks.

Title: Evaluate an adapter before activation and support rollback
User story: As a user, I want a candidate adapter evaluated against the current configuration before activation so that a training job cannot silently worsen my operational translations.
Acceptance criteria:
Compare the candidate with the same base, prompts and reviewed memory on development/promotion cases and a separate retention set. Check equipment ID, action, negation, quantity/unit and sequence. Keep the final research test untouched until R06; do not use final-test results to promote or tune an adapter.
Use an acceptance rule written before viewing candidate results, with a retention check on earlier skills. If the gate fails or evidence is insufficient, keep the previous configuration and explain the result.
An explicit user action can activate a passed candidate only between sessions. Reload its checkpoint after restart and verify adapter/base compatibility and recorded version IDs.
Rollback and delete controls restore the previous validated configuration, with a visible selection and audit record. Successful training is never equated with demonstrated improvement.
Deliverable: Locked evaluation protocol, paired results, review decisions and activate/reload/rollback demonstration.

Title: Compare frozen, glossary and local-memory conditions
User story: As a researcher, I want controlled ablations of the same model so any difference can be attributed to reviewed local information rather than changed models or hidden hints.
Acceptance criteria:
One script reproduces B0 frozen/no local adaptation, B1 same model+approved fixed glossary and B2 same model+retrieved reviewed examples using a pinned configuration and identical source/context.
Use development data to fix prompt/retrieval parameters; log retrieved example IDs and verify no final-test family, answer key or future session appears in the context.
Evaluate the final test only after configuration freeze. Randomize/blind condition labels for bilingual reviewers; retain raw outputs, settings, timings and adjudicated labels.
Primary text measure: messages with any wrong/omitted required critical field or unsupported critical addition divided by evaluated messages. Also report per-field wrong/omitted counts and denominators, additions, adequacy, clarification behavior and resource cost; use the R03 criticality rubric.
If B2 is no better or worse, preserve that result and error analysis; do not select only successful examples or quietly retune on final-test outputs.
Include B3 only if ENG7/ENG8 have produced a compatible validated adapter before the final condition freeze. Record training configuration, duration, resources and retention; otherwise report B3 as not run. Never convert memory updates into a training result.
Deliverable:
Versioned evaluation runner/config
Blinded outputs and reviewer labels
Core ablation table and retrieval-leakage audit

Title: Run a consented exploratory UX and task pilot
User story: As the team, we want observation from actual users so we can identify misunderstandings and usability barriers that software checks cannot reveal.
Acceptance criteria:
Target four consenting pairs (eight adults) suitable for the chosen language task; adjust the pilot size before recruitment if capacity changes. Record language familiarity and experience without unnecessary demographic inference. This is exploratory, not a powered efficacy trial.
Use 1-2 separate dry-run pairs or sessions to fix instructions before the pilot; exclude them from the frozen comparison and document changes.
Compare at most two stable conditions in this small pilot (e.g. B0 versus preselected B2) using matched, unseen scenario variants and balanced AB/BA order across pairs. Do not show the same answer fixture twice to a pair.
Collect task decision correctness, attempted wrong choices/held choices, tagged clarifications, completion times, assistance needed and a short comprehension/usability interview; record failures and withdrawals.
Analyze pair/session-level descriptive evidence and sequence effects. Do not present multiple messages from one pair as independent participants, or claim statistical efficacy from this small convenience sample.
Deliverable:
Pilot protocol/schedule
Consented local session records
Usability findings and task summary

Title: Produce reproducible effectiveness and limitations analysis
User story: As a reviewer, I want transparent results and failure analysis so I can judge what the prototype demonstrates and what remains uncertain.
Acceptance criteria:
Analysis script regenerates all tables/figures from versioned consented or shareable records; checks denominators, missing data, duplicate events and condition/build/transport labels.
Report core outcomes by condition and scenario skill, with raw counts and effect estimates; uncertainty calculations, if used, respect grouped families/pairs rather than treating correlated messages as independent.
Separate automated semantic corpus results, human task/usability observations, device feasibility and existing regression checks into distinct evidence tables.
Include disagreement/adjudication results, counterexamples, negative findings, retention if trained, recruitment/split limitations and any unmet planned milestone.
A second team member reproduces key numbers from the manifest and confirms every paper claim is supported by an artifact.
Deliverable:
Analysis scripts and generated figures
Results/limitations tables
Peer reproduction checklist

Title: Demonstrate the integrated workflow with internet disabled
User story: As a professor reviewing the project, I want a physical-device demonstration and evidence package showing which offline features actually work so that effectiveness claims match the implementation.
Acceptance criteria:
After provisioning, cold-start the local host, local companions and browsers from installed files with WAN/internet disabled; complete a translated round on the two declared supported devices and export. Repeat the declared router/hotspot acceptance checks without relying on cached cloud responses.
Review a consented correction, update only its device's memory and show a subsequent retrieval-assisted translation. Verify the partner's private vault is not uploaded or merged.
If the training gate passed, complete the opt-in local training/evaluation/reload/rollback segment on the eligible laptop with internet disabled. Otherwise explicitly mark that milestone unmet and demonstrate queueing with the recorded reason; do not count it as passed training acceptance.
Publish screenshots/video, outside-network audit, device/resource measurements, regression results and a passed/failed/not-tested feature matrix. Updated manual/report and the paper-ready methods/results distinguish software behavior from measured language or participant benefit.
Deliverable: Physical offline acceptance pack, feature matrix, demonstration recording and updated technical/user documents.

Title: Deliver a paper-ready artifact and invention-review package
User story: As the project team, we want a complete, reviewable outcome package so the professor can assess literature, originality, effectiveness and research outputs.
Acceptance criteria:
Deliver a supervisor-reviewable manuscript with research question, verified related work, implemented method, dataset/consent boundaries, experiments, results, limitations and contributor statement.
Provide a versioned reproducibility pack: source/build/model hashes, dependencies/configs, run instructions, analysis code, synthetic/shareable sample data and an access statement for private data. Never publish private participant records by default.
Update the FactoryRelay proposal/report and standalone manual under research/ so the published simulator and implemented LAN transport are clearly distinguished from local AI/hardware plans; align abstract, slides and demo with measured capabilities.
Link the R11 disclosure decision when applicable. Distinguish manuscript draft, submitted paper, accepted paper, disclosure, application and granted patent. No external submission or disclosure is authorized by completing this planning item.
Professor receives an evidence-to-criterion index, final demo recording/screenshots, team contribution log and an explicit submission-ready versus actually submitted/published status.
Deliverable: Manuscript draft; reproducibility package; final slides/demo; criterion-to-evidence index; contributor record.

Title: Prepare an invention-review brief if the evidence supports one
User story: As the team, I want a specific technical mechanism and its closest overlaps reviewed so any patent route is based on evidence and compatible with publication plans.
Acceptance criteria:
Document the mechanism, technical effect to test, closest paper/patent overlaps, contributors, dated design evidence and unresolved questions.
Prepare a factual invention disclosure or a recorded decision that the current evidence supports a research/artifact contribution rather than a patent claim.
Identify the university technology-transfer contact and request route; record the already-public game/dataset, dated versions and any proposed new disclosure for qualified review. No filing, grant or legal conclusion is promised.
Deliverable: Invention-review brief or documented no-disclosure rationale; institutional-review questions.

Title: Add a bounded local voice input experiment
User story: As a consenting speaker on a supported device, I want a locally transcribed audio draft that I can correct before sharing so that voice can be tested without treating an ASR guess as the original message.
Acceptance criteria:
On one declared device, explicit microphone consent enables local recording and offline ASR; preserve raw audio, ASR draft and user-corrected transcript as distinct consented records. Only the reviewed selected message is shared by default.
Extend the current LAN microphone/CSP restriction only through a deliberate narrow design; test permission refusal, recording stop, deletion and no outside-network audio transfer.
Use speaker-reviewed dialect-faithful references to report WER/CER plus critical operational-field errors and latency on the small declared set. Any synthetic noise trial is labelled separately from real factory recordings.
If the speech model, consent or device gate fails, retain typed communication and report the voice experiment as not implemented or not validated. No speech-training or every-phone support claim follows from text LoRA.
Deliverable: Voice capability record, consent/deletion tests and separate speech evaluation report.

Title: Demonstrate a guarded laboratory action if hardware is approved
User story: As a laboratory supervisor, I want a tightly restricted, human-confirmed action demonstration so that any physical extension remains separate from free-form model output and from claims of industrial deployment.
Acceptance criteria:
Start with a mock or de-energized gateway for one allowlisted action. Model text remains a proposal; a human confirms a structured command and deterministic permissions/fresh-state checks authorize only that bounded action.
Before any energized rig demonstration, the laboratory supervisor approves the independent stop/interlock arrangement and test procedure. Verify rejection of wrong identifiers, stale state, duplicate requests, missing confirmation and network loss under that procedure.
Record attempted, rejected and executed actions separately. The controller's independent protections do not depend on translation correctness, the browser or a language model.
If hardware access or approval is unavailable, deliver the gateway/mock test evidence and explicitly retain the physical demonstration as unachieved. Do not describe OPC UA connectivity or passing mock tests as certified machine safety.
Deliverable: Approved boundary/test sheet, mock gateway results and conditional supervised laboratory record.
